metadata.source: Ontario Building Code (O. Reg. 332/12) + IASR (O. Reg. 191/11) + Impact Assessment Act (S.C. 2019, c. 28) + Constitution Act, 1982 s.35 (Haida Nation, 2004 SCC 73)

metadata.intendedFor: Review of Ontario / Canada building permit, site plan, and environmental review submissions.

rules.naturalLanguage: Newly constructed or redeveloped exterior paths of travel must conform to the IASR (O. Reg. 191/11) Part IV.1 Design of Public Spaces standards. The application must explicitly state IASR / AODA conformance.
rules.remediation: Add to {section.heading}: state conformance with IASR O. Reg. 191/11 Part IV.1 for all exterior paths of travel and accessible parking, including the minimum 1.5 m clear width, 1:20 maximum running slope, and Type A/B accessible parking signage per s. 80.36.
rules.evidenceQuote: Newly constructed or redeveloped exterior paths of travel shall meet the requirements set out in section 80.10.
rules.sourceContent: IASR O. Reg. 191/11, Part IV.1, Design of Public Spaces Standards (Accessibility Standards for the Built Environment), ss. 80.8–80.16. Applies to obligated organizations constructing or redeveloping public spaces in Ontario.

rules.naturalLanguage: Travel distance from any point in a floor area to the nearest exit must comply with Ontario Building Code 3.4.2 limits.
rules.remediation: Add to {section.heading}: state the maximum travel distance from any point in the floor area to the nearest exit and confirm conformance with OBC 3.4.2.
rules.evidenceQuote: Except as permitted by Sentences (2) to (8), the travel distance to the nearest exit shall be not more than ...
rules.sourceContent: Ontario Building Code, O. Reg. 332/12, s. 3.4.2 Exits — limits on travel distance to an exit.

rules.naturalLanguage: Buildings of the major occupancies and sizes triggered by OBC 3.2.2 must be sprinklered to NFPA 13.
rules.remediation: Add to {section.heading}: confirm fully-sprinklered design per OBC 3.2.2 and reference NFPA 13.
rules.evidenceQuote: Sprinklered throughout in conformance with NFPA 13 ...
rules.sourceContent: Ontario Building Code, O. Reg. 332/12, s. 3.2.2 Building Size and Construction Relative to Occupancy. NFPA 13 — Standard for the Installation of Sprinkler Systems.

rules.naturalLanguage: The federal Impact Assessment Act, S.C. 2019, c. 28 prohibits any proponent from carrying out a designated project until an impact assessment is complete (s. 9). The application must address whether the project is designated and, if so, attest to IAA compliance.
rules.lambda: input1.text.Contains("Impact Assessment Act") || input1.text.Contains("IAAC") || input1.text.Contains("Physical Activities Regulations") || (input1.text.Contains("designated project") && input1.text.Contains("federal"))
rules.remediation: Add to {section.heading}: state whether the project is a 'designated project' under the Physical Activities Regulations (SOR/2019-285) and, if so, the IAAC file reference.
rules.evidenceQuote: 9 No proponent of a designated project shall do any act or thing in connection with the carrying out of the designated project ... until ...
rules.sourceContent: Impact Assessment Act, S.C. 2019, c. 28, s. 9 (prohibition); Physical Activities Regulations SOR/2019-285 (definition of designated projects).

rules.naturalLanguage: Where Crown conduct may adversely affect asserted or established Aboriginal or treaty rights, the Crown owes a duty to consult under s. 35 of the Constitution Act, 1982 (Haida Nation v. British Columbia, 2004 SCC 73). Permit applications that could trigger Crown action affecting such rights must address consultation.
rules.lambda: input1.text.Contains("duty to consult") || input1.text.Contains("consultation and accommodation") || (input1.text.Contains("section 35") && input1.text.Contains("Constitution"))
rules.remediation: Add to {section.heading}: identify Indigenous communities whose rights or interests may be affected, summarise consultation undertaken, and reference the duty to consult under s. 35.
rules.evidenceQuote: The duty arises when the Crown has knowledge, real or constructive, of the potential existence of the Aboriginal right or title and contemplates conduct that might adversely affect it.
rules.sourceContent: Constitution Act, 1982, s. 35; Haida Nation v. British Columbia (Minister of Forests), 2004 SCC 73.
